div.p: The increasing scope, demand, scalable virtual environment and advancement in cloud computing infrastructure has led to the association of real time tasks in cloud computing. In Real Time systems, the execution of the tasks is performed on remote virtual machines, the loose control over these virtual computing nodes results in increased probability of errors and therefore poses challenges like reliability, timeliness, QoS requirements and Fault Tolerance. This paper evaluates the execution of real time tasks in cloud computing environment by analysing Fault Tolerance models running real time applications and their associated drawbacks. Also the challenges of implementing real time tasks in cloud environment have been reviewed.

div.head: INTRODUCTION
div.p: Cloud can be contemplated as a dynamic environment where resources are presented by the Cloud Service Provider (CSP). Cloud computing provides pervasive, appropriate, on-demand network access services to the users. Fault tolerance may be defined as the capability of the system to endure the Generally software fault tolerance is considered as it helps in improving reliability of the system without any involvement of hardware cost. A Real Time system may be defined as the system in which there is necessity of quantifiable expression of time (i.e.

real-time) to describe the behavior of the system. In these systems the perfection of the produced results depends on the logical result of computation as well as on the time at which the results are produced[l].

We cannot consider that a real time system runs quickly but it is a system that has time-based constraints to fulfill. An important time constraint is the deadline associated with system. Deadline of a particular task may be defined as the time limit in which task must be completed and appropriate results must be produced. Delay and duration are the other types of time constraints. A real time system has various applications to perform. An application is further divided into number of real time tasks. Types of real time tasks are:

div.head: A.) Hard Real Time Tasks
div.p: These tasks are constrained to produce their results within specified, predetermined times. Applications are anti-missile systems and robots.

div.head: B.) Soft Real Time Tasks
div.p: Timing constraints are linked with these kind of tasks but in this case some tasks can miss their deadlines.

div.head: II. CLOUD COMPUTING AND REAL TIME TASKS
div.p: A real time system is to function precisely within the allotted time. If we compare Real time system with the general purpose system, a Real time system needs to function appropriately so that it gives correct and accurate results within the timing constraints [2,3].
Various kinds of errors, faults and failures can occur in the real time systems [4,5]. Fault Tolerance in Real Time(RT) tasks is to deal with this.

Since cloud is very elastic in nature according to user requirements; Hence Fault tolerance for real-time tasks is a major challenging issue in cloud environment. There are various real time applications deployed in cloud computing like Real Time Weather Forecast [6], RT Signal Processing [8] and RT Image Processing [7] .

div.head: Drawbacks:
div.p: In this scheduler model one major drawback is the disturbing of QOS Levels of the tasks residing in the local queue. Whenever a task arrives , the QoS level of this task is compared with the tasks previously present in the local queue. If its QoS level is less than that of all the tasks in queue then the QoS levels of the tasks in local queue is decreased in order to increase QoS level of new task [19]. Hence it results in recalculation of start times of the tasks. Hence more overhead is associated in maintaining QoS level of all the tasks.

In order to successfully execute the task ,the backup copy of the task can be executed on a different VM if the primary copy of the task gets failed [20]. The backup copy can be in active mode or passive which depends on the time at which backup copy begins its execution.

div.head: Real time scheduling of virtual machines
div.p: The issue is of performance isolation in which appropriate scheduling algorithms for the isolated virtual machines in cloud Infrastructure need to be considered [22].

• Resource Management-Due to increase in resource sharing among the virtual machines the performance of a particular VM is not only dependent on its own resource consumption but also on the no. of resources consumed by other virtual machines. FUTURE DIRECTIONS Future work is two fold : (l) to resolve all the above examined challenges of executing real time tasks in cloud computing; (2) to propose a model that considers reliability, QoS, service requirements together to achieve fault tolerance.CONCLUSIONAs the real time applications have been associated with cloud environment it becomes necessary for cloud infrastructure to fulfill QoS requirements including reliability, availability, timeliness and service requirements of the applications to achieve fault tolerance. There is necessity of a solution that combines management and deployment of VM's that runs real time tasks with QoS needs of applications to achieve successful result. In this paper an enlightened view of benefits of executing RT tasks in cloud environment along with FT models for real time tasks in cloud computing and challenges of performing these tasks in cloud computing is presented. Hence more work is needed in this field to resolve the examined issues.
